description: ARG CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY default is baked into the image ENV (lines 12,30); deploys that do not override it encrypt all stored third-party credentials under a publicly known key.
Heroku one-click deploy template ships a default CALENDSO_ENCRYPTION_KEY value; deployers keeping the default encrypt every stored credential with a publicly known hard-coded key.
symmetricEncrypt/Decrypt use unauthenticated AES-256-CBC (ALGORITHM=aes256) with a raw latin1 key and no auth tag, so stored credential ciphertext is malleable (tamper/padding-oracle risk).
PbacGuard.canActivate returns true even when required permissions are absent (sets pbacAuthorizedRequest=false), delegating denial to a downstream RolesGuard; routes using it alone fail open.
Edge middleware redirects to the return-to cookie value via NextResponse.redirect(new URL(returnTo.value,...)); an attacker-influenced cookie with an absolute URL yields an open redirect.
Outbound webhook POSTs server-side fetch to the user-registered subscriberUrl; a URL pointing at internal hosts or cloud metadata enables SSRF (redirect:manual only limits redirect-based pivots).
CRON_API_KEY is committed with a hard-coded value in the env template; deployers copying .env.example keep a known key that authorizes privileged /api/cron endpoints (cron job trigger abuse).
Workflow uses third-party action lingodotdev/lingo.dev@main (mutable branch) in a job with contents+pull-requests write plus app token and API key; a malicious update gains repo write and secrets.
ARG NEXTAUTH_SECRET default is baked into the image ENV (lines 11,29); deploys not overriding it let an attacker forge NextAuth JWTs and take over any session.
Heroku deploy template sets PGSSLMODE=no-verify, disabling Postgres TLS certificate verification and exposing the database connection to man-in-the-middle interception.
Inbound Vercel promote webhook is verified with HMAC-SHA1, a deprecated weak hash versus HMAC-SHA256 used outbound; timingSafeEqual and a length check are present so practical risk is low.
Session impersonation linkage is rebuilt from the token.impersonatedBy claim; its integrity rests solely on NEXTAUTH_SECRET, so a forged or default secret lets an attacker impersonate any user.
messageParent posts embed data to the parent window with targetOrigin '*', so booking/embed messages are delivered without restricting the receiving origin.
Iframe message handler invokes interfaceWithParent[method] after only checking data.originator==='CAL' and never validates event.origin; any page framing the embed can drive internal methods.
postMessage to iframe.contentWindow uses targetOrigin '*' (TODO at line 407 acknowledges it); embed control messages can be read by any origin occupying the frame.
Parent-side message listener fires action-manager events from e.data without validating e.origin; a malicious page can spoof Cal embed events (e.g. booking callbacks) to the host site.
Gateway proxies all non-/v2 traffic to legacy v1 (Next.js) while /v2 uses the NestJS three-ring guards; divergent authZ/validation between versions can let v1 expose resources with weaker checks.

Version extractor silently defaults to VERSION_2024_04_15 when the cal-api-version header is missing or invalid; clients can omit the header to obtain an older version's potentially weaker validation.
Global ValidationPipe sets validationError.value=true, echoing submitted field values back in 400 error responses, which can disclose sensitive request data through error output.
Production script-src appends 'unsafe-inline' https: as a fallback alongside nonce/strict-dynamic; browsers without strict-dynamic support honor unsafe-inline, weakening XSS protection.
getCspHeader emits an enforcing Content-Security-Policy only when shouldEnforceCsp is true (login routes); all other pages receive no CSP header because the report-only path is commented out.
